To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a folate- and methionine-deficient diet alters expression of DNA methylation machinery components, which may contribute to the epigenetic silencing of tumor-suppressor genes during early stages of carcinogenesis.
a folate and methyl deficient diet alters the expression and activity of DNA methyltransferase and methyl CpG-binding proteins involved in DNA methylation in rat livers.
a folate- and methionine-deficient diet alters DNA methylation machinery in rat livers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying aberrations in DNA methylation profile of genome during early stages of carcinogenesis induced by folate and methyl deficiencies.
understanding the mechanisms by which a combined methyl and folate deficiency induces aberrant DNA methylation and gene silencing in rat livers.
understanding how the folate and methionine deficiency affects the DNA methylation system in the liver and how these changes contribute to the development of hepatocellular carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA methylation profile in the genome is affected by a folate and methyl deficient diet, and that this effect may play a significant role in carcinogenesis.
a combined folater and methyl deficiency alters the expression of Dnmt1 and MBD2 in a posttranscriptional manner.
a diet deficient in folate, methyl, and choline induces alterations in DNA methylation machinery in rat liver, which may be involved in epigenetically mediated carcinogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

folate deficiency induces DNA hypomethylation in rat liver and this is associated with an increase in the expression of the methyl CpG binding protein MBD1 and the maintenance DNA methyltransferases, Dnmt1 and Dnmt3A.
a combined folater and methyl deficiency results in an increased expression of the DNA methlytransferases and MBDs, which may contribute to an aberrant DNA methylation profile and carcinogenesis.

a combined folatedeficiency and methionine deficiency alters the expression of Dnmts, MBDs and MeCP2 in rat liver during early stages of carcinogenesis and these changes are likely to be associated with the aberrant methylation of genes in the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a folate and methyl deficient diet alters components of the epigenetic machinery in the liver, which may play a role in the initiation of liver tumorigenesis in the F344 rat model of hepatocarcininogenesis.
folate and methyl deficiencies alter the DNA methylation apparatus in the liver, and this may be one of the mechanisms underlying the development of hepatocellular cancer.
the aberrant expression of these proteins may be a contributing factor to aberrant DNA methylation patterns observed in folate deficiency.
